 Kingston Flemings (back) will not return to Friday’s game against the Bulls. 
 Initially questionable for Friday’s game with a back injury, Flemings played 17 minutes before the issue flared up and ended his night. The rookie guard finished with zero points, one rebound and one assist while looking uncomfortable throughout. CJ McCollum has been tabbed to fill the void, rejoining the starters. 
 Kingston Flemings 
 ATL 
 Guard 
 #4 
 Kingston Flemings (back) is questionable to play against the Bulls on Friday. 
 Flemings could miss a game due to injury for the first time in his career. If he ends up sidelined, CJ McCollum will likely make a return to the starting unit. 
 Kingston Flemings 
 ATL 
 Guard 
 #4 
 Kingston Flemings supplied 10 points (5-of-8 FGs), two rebounds and two blocks across 27 minutes in a win over the Nets on Saturday. 
 Flemings has fit rather seamlessly into Atlanta’s starting lineup, taking the place of veteran CJ McCollum for the third consecutive game. He managed to reach double figures in the scoring department for the third straight contest as he took more of a backseat with Jalen Johnson back from a sprained ankle. The 19-year-old rookie has put himself on fantasy managers’ radar screens with his recent performance and should be rostered in deeper leagues. 
 Kingston Flemings 
 ATL 
 Guard 
 #4 
 Kingston Flemings had 14 points (6-of-9 FGs), three rebounds, four assists, and two 3-pointers in win over the Wizards. 
 In his first start of his career, he played well and you felt his imprint on the game. It was said on the broadcast that it was CJ McCollum’s idea for Kingston to start and get into a rhythm. It is notable that Kingston played 23 minutes when CJ played 25 minutes. His ability to collapse a defense with his speed was on full display. We’ll see if this is a permanent change, but he clearly looked good in this game. 
 Kingston Flemings 
 ATL 
 Guard 
 #4 
 Kingston Flemings, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, Luguentz Dort and Onyeka Okongwu will start Wednesday’s game against the Wizards. 
 Jalen Johnson (ankle) will miss a second straight game, so Dort remains in the starting lineup. The other change is big: Flemings has replaced CJ McCollum. The change boosts the rookie’s fantasy value, especially if head coach Quin Snyder sticks with it moving forward. 
 Kingston Flemings 
 ATL 
 Guard 
 #4 
 Kingston Flemings has been suspended one game for his actions during Saturday’s loss to the Pelicans. 
 Flemings was ejected from Saturday’s game after elbowing Pelicans wing Bryce McGowens in the face during a confrontation. The NBA has since suspended the rookie for one game, which he’ll serve on Monday against the Pacers. Flemings will be eligible to return on Wednesday against the Wizards. 
 Kingston Flemings 
 ATL 
 Guard 
 #4 
 Kingston Flemings was ejected from Saturday’s game against the Pelicans with 3:04 remaining in the fourth quarter. 
 Flemings was ejected after an altercation with New Orleans’ Bryce McGowens. After McGowens blocked Flemings’ layup attempt, the rookie guard threw an elbow at the face of the Pelicans’ wing while play headed in the opposite direction. Multiple players from both teams left their benches, but no one else was ejected because the Hawks had called a timeout. Flemings finished with 12 points, two rebounds, six assists, four steals and one three-pointer. 
 Kingston Flemings 
 ATL 
 Guard 
 #4 
 Kingston Flemings had 23 points (9-of-12 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers against the Heat on Wednesday. 
 Flemings came off the bench, played 28 minutes and had the best game of his young career so far. The 19-year-old rookie was impressive with 23 points on 12 attempts from the field and a full stat line. Flemings ended up playing more minutes than starter CJ McCollum, but don’t expect that to continue. Timing Flemings’ next outstanding performance will be difficult given his inconsistent playing time, making him more of a priority in dynasty formats. 
 CJ McCollum 
 ATL 
 Guard 
 #3 
 CJ McCollum posted 14 points (5-of-11 FGs), five rebounds, four assists and four three-pointers in Thursday’s exhibition against the Spurs. 
 After sitting out Atlanta’s preseason opener, McCollum played on Thursday, and his insertion into the lineup pushed Kingston Flemings (15/3/5/3, with two three-pointers) to the bench. McCollum’s move to the starting lineup was a major reason the Hawks finished the 2025-26 regular season with a flourish, and he’ll have a similar role this season. While his fantasy ceiling is somewhat limited, McCollum’s floor should be safe. 
 Kingston Flemings 
 ATL 
 Guard 
 Kingston Flemings notched 11 points (4-of-11 FGs, 1-of-4 FTs) and two assists over 24 minutes during Monday’s preseason loss to the Grizzlies. 
 Flemings, the eighth-overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, will back up veteran CJ McCollum who is back on a one-year, $21 million pact following a stellar postseason performance. The 19-year-old rookie got the start in Atlanta’s pre-season lid-lifter with McCollum getting the night off. There are plenty of mouths to feed in the Hawks’ new-look backcourt, but Flemings should have the green light whenever he comes off the bench, especially since they don’t have a ton of high-volume scorers in their present nucleus. He’ll go undrafted in most redraft leagues, but he’s likely to have some moments throughout his rookie season where he shows some flashes of big-time scoring upside.

 Aday Mara recorded 10 points (5-of-6 FGs), three rebounds and three blocks in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
 While Mara has started four of Oklahoma City’s last six games, the 21 minutes he logged on Friday were the least he’s played in any of those starts. There were some positives to the rookie’s performance, specifically the field-goal percentage and blocked shots. However, Mara hasn’t done enough with Chet Holmgren (knee) out to become a player who has to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

 Isaiah Hartenstein notched 21 points (9-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 16 rebounds, six assists and one steal in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
 After scoring no more than seven points in any of Oklahoma City’s first five games in November, Hartenstein has scored at least 20 in two straight games. He was outstanding against the Clippers, shooting 90 percent from the field and providing excellent value in points, rebounds and assists. Providing top-100 fantasy value, Hartenstein is rostered in 84 percent of Yahoo leagues. Given Oklahoma City’s frontcourt injuries, those rostering Hartenstein would be better served holding on to him than entertaining a trade after the last two games.

 Jared McCain tallied 23 points (8-of-17 FGs), four rebounds, two assists and seven three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
 McCain has scored in double figures in four straight games, with Friday’s being the best of the bunch. The Thunder guard shot 7-of-11 from deep against the Clippers, recording season highs in points and three-pointers. McCain will mainly be a “points and triples” option in fantasy leagues, but Oklahoma City’s injuries open the door for him to provide consistent value.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Friday’s loss to the Clippers with 40 points (15-of-26 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
 Gilgeous-Alexander finished with his third 40-point game of the season, but he wishes he’d scored 42 instead of 40. The two-time MVP’s shot as time expired missed the mark, resulting in a 113-112 Clippers victory. After shooting a combined 17-of-42 in two losses to the Trail Blazers, Gilgeous-Alexander was much more efficient on Friday, shooting well over 50 percent from the field. He could be in for another big night to end the week, as the Thunder visit the Kings on Sunday.

 After reaching double figures in each of his first five games, Wagler totaled 13 points on 4-of-13 shooting in the Clippers’ first two games of November. The rookie has gotten back on track, having scored at least 11 points in four straight games. Wagler remains a deep-league option in redraft formats, while dynasty league managers should be excited for the rookie guard’s future.

 Derrick Jones Jr. accounted for 14 points (5-of-10 FGs), five rebounds, one steal, four blocks and four three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
 Thanks mainly to the three-pointers and defensive stats, Jones has been close to a top-100 player in nine-cat formats. Against the Thunder, he shot 4-of-7 from beyond the arc and recorded five “stocks” in 29 minutes. This was Jones’ fourth game this season with at least two three-pointers, one steal and one block. Managers needing help in those categories should consider adding Jones ahead of Sunday’s game against the Hornets.

 Brook Lopez accumulated 26 points (11-of-21 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
 After coming off the bench in the Clippers’ first six games, Lopez is approaching the point where he needs to be rostered in 12-team leagues. He’s scored at least 20 points in three of the last four games, with Friday’s total being a season high. Add in the rebounds and three-pointers, and this was a good night for those rostering the veteran center. Isaiah Jackson (5/3/3 with one block), who began the season as the starter, should be rostered only in very deep leagues.

 Darius Garland finished Friday’s win over the Thunder with 24 points (8-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, one block and three three-pointers.
 After being outscored 40-25 in the third quarter, Garland and the Clippers did what needed to be done down the stretch to win the 113-112 thriller. The Clippers’ starting point guard had the game’s biggest shot: a layup through contact and an ensuing free throw with 50.4 seconds left to take the lead for good. Even with the occasional struggles with turnovers, Garland is providing top-100 fantasy value through 11 games. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 After a really bad game against the Magic, Sabonis bounced back and went back to his usual self against the Blazers. He looked healthier in this game, which is a good sign. The efficiency has still been good, but it is starting to come down from his super-hot start. He still puts up good counting stats which is why you have Sabonis in the first place. Overall, its been a good season so far.
